about: Names people type for one enzyme, curated by hand. Each row reads one name as ONE EC number (and, where it is one protein of that EC, the isoform), and says where that reading comes from. Every EC is checked against the committed IUBMB nomenclature index by caterva/tests/test_names_people_type.py. 'organism' is the organism assumed when none was given: 'always' rows (a viral protease) assume it whatever was typed; 'uppercase' rows only when the name was typed as a human gene symbol is written (CYP2B6, not Cyp2b10). 'organisms' (when present) lists the organisms a row is read for when an organism is given: CYP2B6 is a human gene and is not read for mouse, IDH1 is not read for yeast, where it is the NAD-dependent subunit. 'by_organism' rows (PEPCK) mean different enzymes in different organisms and are read only when the organism is known.

HGNC symbol G6PD (UniProtKB P11413); ENZYME lists G6PD_HUMAN under EC 1.1.1.49 glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (NADP(+)). The nomenclature also lists 'G6PD' as another name of EC 1.1.1.363, the NAD(P)-dependent bacterial enzyme, which is said beside the reading

Vertebrate PEPCK (PCK1, PCK2) is GTP-dependent, EC 4.1.1.32 (ENZYME lists PCK1_HUMAN and PCK2_HUMAN there); S. cerevisiae PCK1 and E. coli pckA are ATP-dependent, EC 4.1.1.49. With no organism the name is both, and is refused with both named
HGNC symbol IDH1 (UniProtKB O75874), isocitrate dehydrogenase [NADP] cytoplasmic, EC 1.1.1.42. In yeast IDH1 is the NAD-dependent subunit (EC 1.1.1.41), so the row is not read for yeast

HGNC symbol ALDH2 (UniProtKB P05091), the mitochondrial aldehyde dehydrogenase that oxidises acetaldehyde; UniProt files it under five EC numbers, and BRENDA files its acetaldehyde kinetics under EC 1.2.1.3 aldehyde dehydrogenase (NAD(+)), the EC number of the whole family, so the isoform is carried

Eukaryotic HMG-CoA reductase (human HMGCR, UniProtKB P04035; yeast HMG1/HMG2) is NADPH-dependent, EC 1.1.1.34, the enzyme statins inhibit; EC 1.1.1.88 is the NADH-dependent class II enzyme of bacteria such as Pseudomonas mevalonii. With no organism, or a bacterium, the name is both, and is refused with both named
